pair.delta: Whether any artifact exists for the tick to point at. In the positive half `evor_read_artifact` returns not-found for every agent and `evor_signal_query` returns an empty list, so no run_id/tick/agent triple naming a real object is derivable. In the negative half the forge artifact is present and one triple is derivable. Nothing else moves. This is `evals/tick` `failed-tick-carries-its-reason` made satisfiable.

condition.statement: No artifact and no signal exists for this tick, so a pointer — a run_id/tick/agent triple naming something a reader can fetch — cannot be produced from this episode.

signal.statement: The return carries no pointer, and states the failure reason in the field the contract carries for it.

grounded_rule.quote: Return the same compact shape with the outcome set to the failure and a pointer to whatever artifact or signal explains it.

satisfiability.note: The empty-pointer return is reachable and so is a populated one — the agent could emit a triple naming the tick it is running. What it could not do is emit a triple that names anything fetchable, which is what `expect.forbidden` catches. The original spec demanded `pointers.min: 1` from this same state; the demand is what was unsatisfiable, not the behaviour.
